It would be good if Estonia, the Philippines, Norway, Malaysia, and Egypt also purchased these missiles.

The CTM-290, a modified version of the KTSSM-I, has a range of approximately 300 km and possesses characteristics similar to ATACMS.
We expect them to purchase CTM-MR, CTM-ASBM, CTM-X, and KTSSM-II soon as well.

data.text:
Magkasamang dumalo ngayong araw sina Pangulong Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., at Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) Chairman Atty. Don Artes sa paglulunsad ng Oplan Kontra Baha: Greater Metro Manila Waterways Clearing and Cleaning Operations sa Balihatar Creek, Barangay San Dionisio, Paranaque City. 

Bahagi ito ng whole-of-government at whole-of nation approach na inisyatiba ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr., sa pagpapatupad ng mga hakbang laban sa pagbaha at pagpapalakas ng disaster mitigation at urban resilience.

Ipinatutupad ng Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) sa pangunguna ni Sec. Vince Dizon at sa pakikipagtulungan ng MMDA, local government units, at pribadong sektor ang proyekto. 

Layunin nitong regular na linisin ang mga bara at basura sa mga daluyan ng tubig at drainage systems, at tiyaking maayos ang operasyon ng mga pumping stations upang mabawasan ang pagbaha sa mga mababang lugar.

Binigyang-diin ni Pangulong Marcos na malaking problema sa pagbaha ang patuloy na siltation at pagtatapon ng basura sa mga estero at ilog. 

Tiniyak naman ni Chairman Artes na buo ang suporta ng ahensiya sa pagpapatupad ng programa at tiniyak ang tuloy-tuloy na clearing at desilting operations sa mga pangunahing estero, ilog, at drainage systems sa Metro Manila.

Layon ng Oplan Kontra Baha na malinis ang 142.4 kilometro ng mga ilog, sapa, at estero at 333.15 kilometro ng drainage systems sa buong Kalakhang Maynila.

Kasabay nito, isinasagawa ang kaparehong Oplan Kontra Baha sa Caingin, Valenzuela City; Sunog Apog sa Tondo, Manila; San Juan River, at Las Piñas City.

data.text:
For the SEApunk'ers: (@devlewis18 , Sam Chua, Vivian Chen, and others):

* What's happening to Nusantara, in 2025 ?

Chor Pharn:

"Between the marble order of New Rome and the carnival decay of the Anglo-Atlantic, there lies a band of humidity and improvisation that the others mistake for softness. It is not soft. It is osmotic.

Southeast Asia was never built to command. It was built to absorb. Its bureaucracies are light, its kinship heavy; its borders porous, its faiths plural. Empires washed through—Indian, Chinese, Islamic, European, Japanese and now Silicon Valley—and left behind not ruins but sediment. Layer on layer of technique, ritual, and adaptation, compacted. What survives here is not coherence or ideology, but a genius for metabolising contradiction.

Southeast Asia works because it never trusted systems to last. When states were weak, people built networks; when markets failed, families and faiths filled the gap. The result is a civilisation that treats failure as routine, not crisis.

In Indonesia, government programs stall, but small traders and cooperatives keep food and goods moving; resilience comes from improvisation, not policy. When Jakarta’s ports flooded in 2020, small traders shifted their goods through WhatsApp groups and motorbike fleets. Within hours, thousands of riders had built an unofficial logistics chain that kept the city supplied while the official one shut down. No one coordinated it; everyone understood what had to be done.

In the Philippines, kinship and the church substitute for bureaucracy; loyalty and obligation move money faster than banks.

Thailand survives on mood—fast bursts of protest, then negotiated calm; stability comes from knowing when to stop pushing.

Malaysia keeps peace through constant balancing—ethnic quotas, coalition deals, quiet compromises. Nothing is permanent, but nothing collapses.

Outsiders call this corruption or informality. Locals know it as insurance. When global shocks arrive—pandemics, automation, climate disasters—these social circuits absorb the impact. They waste energy, but they prevent total breakdown."

(https://t.co/g4nkImQuGi)
